setup.command: torchtitan_recipes.models.llama3.llama3_8b(seq_len=8192) under GraphTrainer (aot joint fwd+bwd graph, memory_policy='none', regional_inductor with no regions, custom codegen), FSDP 8 via fake process group (rank 0 only), 8192 tokens/microbatch, 1 microbatch/step, deterministic, no AC, no local_compile, no CUDA graphs; profiled step 10 after 3 warmup steps (Kineto trace iteration_10)

regions.title: SwiGLU forward+backward pair: recompute silu in backward instead of saving it
regions.description: With fused SwiGLU forward and backward kernels, the forward no longer needs to write silu(gate) [8192,14336] bf16 and the backward no longer reads it, since the backward kernel already reads gate; this pairs the forward and backward of each feed_forward.
regions.bitwise_notes: Recomputing silu in fp32 then rounding to bf16 reproduces the saved value exactly.
regions.dataflow: forward silu output is saved only for backward mul(dY, silu); the backward kernel reads gate anyway.
regions.blockers: memory_policy 'none' saves every forward activation; changing what is saved is a joint forward/backward decision.
regions.notes: Incremental over the two separate SwiGLU regions: 2 x 234.9MB per layer (about 68us per layer, 2.2ms per step).

regions.title: Weight-grad GEMM epilogues writing fp32 directly into the reduce-scatter bucket
regions.description: The four weight-gradient GEMMs of each block (wqkv, wo, w13, w2) can store their results, rounded to bf16 and widened to fp32, straight into their rank-major slots of the reduce-scatter buffer, removing the cast, re-layout and pack copies.
regions.fusion_kind: GEMM epilogue with scattered fp32 store
regions.bitwise_notes: Bitwise if the epilogue rounds to bf16 before widening.
regions.dataflow: mm(wgrad) -> _to_copy -> (cat) -> _pre_bucket_reduce_scatter -> reduce_scatter.
regions.blockers: GEMM output must be split into 8 rank chunks at arbitrary row (and for w13, Shard(1) dim) boundaries; norm-weight grads come from a different kernel.
regions.notes: Superset of the reduce-scatter pack region; GEMM part measured below the random-data peak.

regions.title: w2 input-gradient GEMM with SwiGLU-backward epilogue
regions.description: The w2 input-gradient GEMM [8192,4096]x[4096,14336] produces dY for SwiGLU; its epilogue can read gate, up and silu for the same tile and write the stacked [8192,2,14336] gradient directly.
regions.bitwise_notes: Bitwise if dY is rounded to bf16 in the epilogue before the SwiGLU backward math.
regions.dataflow: mm(dout, W2) -> dY -> mul/mul/silu_backward/stack -> w13 backward GEMMs; dY is also needed by the w2 wgrad GEMM (mm(mul_out^T... ) uses dout, not dY), so dY has no other consumer.
regions.blockers: Custom epilogue GEMM reading three extra operands per tile.

regions.title: FSDP reduce-scatter pack: weight-grad fp32 casts, w13 re-layout and bucket copy
regions.description: After each decoder block's backward, its six bf16 weight gradients (wqkv 6144x4096, wo 4096x4096, w13 2x14336x4096, w2 4096x14336, two 4096 norm weights) are cast to fp32 one by one, the w13 gradient is re-laid out rank-major with a second full copy, and everything is copied again into the flat fp32 reduce-scatter buffer; one kernel can read each bf16 gradient once and write fp32 straight into its rank-major slot of the buffer.
regions.bitwise_notes: Pure cast (bf16->fp32 is exact) plus copies; the only constraint is reproducing the exact rank-major placement of each element in the bucket, which is deterministic index math.
regions.dataflow: mm(wgrad, bf16) -> _to_copy(f32) [-> view [2,14336,4096] -> split(1792,dim1) -> cat(dim0) for w13] -> _pre_bucket_reduce_scatter (chunk_cat into f32[8*27264000]) -> reduce_scatter. Every intermediate has exactly one consumer, so the chain collapses to a single gather-cast-scatter.
regions.blockers: The cast, the w13 re-layout and the bucket copy come from three layers of software (FSDP grad redistribute, the DTensor Shard(1) placement of w13, and the bucketing pass); a fused kernel needs the bucket layout (per-rank offsets) at graph-pass time. The w13 Shard(1) placement is what forces the extra re-layout copy.
regions.notes: The pack node is annotated with the block's wqkv module but packs all six parameters of the block. The w13 'cat' alone runs at 2.9x its own roofline (non-vectorized CatArrayBatchedCopy on fp32).

regions.title: SwiGLU backward: two muls + silu_backward + stack
regions.description: In each feed_forward backward, the gradient of silu(gate)*up ([8192,14336] bf16) is computed by two separate multiplies, a silu_backward and a stack that interleaves d_gate/d_up into [8192,2,14336]; one elementwise kernel can read dY, gate, up and the saved silu once and write the stacked gradient directly.
regions.fusion_kind: elementwise chain + stack into strided output
regions.bitwise_notes: Pointwise only; must keep aten's rounding points (silu value rounded to bf16 before dY*silu; dY*up rounded to bf16 before silu_backward).
regions.dataflow: mul(dY, silu_saved) -> d_up; mul(dY, up) -> silu_backward(., gate) -> d_gate; stack([d_gate, d_up], -2) -> w13 backward GEMMs. All intermediates single-use.
regions.blockers: None structural; the strided gate/up halves (unbind of the fused w13 output) are what make the separate aten kernels fall back to the slow non-vectorized path.
regions.notes: mul(dY, up) and silu_backward read the stride-28672 halves and run at ~2.8-3.1x roofline; the contiguous mul(dY, silu) runs at roofline.

regions.title: w13 GEMM with SwiGLU epilogue
regions.description: The fused gate/up projection [8192,4096]x[4096,28672] can compute silu(gate)*up in its epilogue (pairing gate and up columns in the same tile), writing the product next to the gate/up output kept for backward.
regions.bitwise_notes: Bitwise if the epilogue rounds gate/up to bf16 first and evaluates silu and the product with aten's rounding points.
regions.dataflow: mm(w13) -> view [8192,2,14336] -> unbind -> silu, mul -> w2 GEMM.
regions.blockers: Tile must cover matching gate and up columns (they are 14336 columns apart in the fused weight); custom epilogue GEMM.

regions.title: SwiGLU forward: silu + mul on the strided gate/up halves of the w13 output
regions.description: Each feed_forward applies silu to the gate half and multiplies by the up half of the fused w13 output [8192,2,14336] bf16 in two kernels that both read stride-28672 views; one kernel can read gate/up once and write silu (kept for backward) and the product.
regions.bitwise_notes: Pointwise; product must use the bf16-rounded silu value as aten does.
regions.dataflow: mm(w13) -> view [8192,2,14336] -> unbind -> silu(gate) ; mul(silu, up) -> w2 GEMM. silu output also saved for backward (memory_policy none).
regions.blockers: None structural.
regions.notes: Both kernels run on non-contiguous views (elementwise_kernel<128,4>, 4.1x and 2.8x roofline). Ideal keeps the silu output write because backward consumes it; see the forward-backward region for dropping it.

regions.title: lm_head GEMM + cross-entropy + input-gradient GEMM per chunk (logits never written)
regions.description: For each 1024-token chunk, the lm_head projection to 128256-way logits, the cross-entropy and its gradient, and the input-gradient GEMM can run as one fused linear-cross-entropy kernel that keeps the logits tile on chip, instead of writing and re-reading [1024,128256] bf16/fp32 tensors five times.
regions.bitwise_notes: Online-softmax reductions change the reduction order versus cunn_SoftMaxForward; bitwise identity would require replicating the row-wise reduction tree across vocab tiles, which is hard.
regions.dataflow: mm(h, W^T) -> CE chain (R: chunked CE) -> mm(dlogits, W) -> dh; the wgrad GEMM (dlogits^T h) also needs dlogits, so either it is fused too (recompute logits per tile) or dlogits is still written once.
regions.blockers: The wgrad GEMM needs dlogits for all vocab rows; a fused kernel must either also produce dW (accumulating across chunks) or still write dlogits once. Bitwise parity with the unfused softmax is unlikely.
regions.notes: Ideal counts only the two GEMMs it absorbs (forward logits and input gradient) at the bf16 peak; measured includes those GEMMs plus the CE chain. GEMMs run below the random-data peak here.

regions.title: Chunked cross-entropy: logits cast, log_softmax, NLL and their backward per 1024-token chunk
regions.description: For each of the 8 chunks of 1024 tokens, the bf16 logits [1024,128256] are cast to fp32, log-softmaxed, NLL-reduced, and immediately differentiated (nll_loss_backward zero-fill + scatter, log_softmax backward, cast back to bf16) in 6 large and 4 scalar kernels; a single kernel can read the bf16 logits once and emit the loss contribution and the bf16 logit gradient.
regions.bitwise_notes: Row max / sum-exp reductions must use the same reduction order as cunn_SoftMaxForward; the gradient (exp(logp)*sum(g) - g) then follows pointwise; the per-chunk loss scalar adds must keep chunk order.
regions.dataflow: mm(lm_head) bf16 -> _to_copy f32 -> _log_softmax (saved) -> nll_loss_forward -> div(token count) -> add (loss accumulator); ones_like -> div -> nll_loss_backward (memset 525MB + scatter) -> _log_softmax_backward_data -> _to_copy bf16 -> lm_head backward GEMMs. The backward for chunk i runs right after its forward, so the fp32 log-probs never need to leave the kernel.
regions.blockers: The chunk's backward is driven by autograd inside the loss forward; fusing forward and backward needs the upstream gradient scale (1/token count) available at forward time, which it is in this joint graph.
regions.notes: Even without the forward-backward fusion, fusing the forward (cast+log_softmax+nll) and the backward (nll_bwd+log_softmax_bwd+cast) separately would remove most of the gap; nll_loss_backward's 525MB zero-fill alone is 78us per chunk.

regions.title: Weight unpack folded into GEMM operand loads (consume the all-gather buffer in place)
regions.description: Instead of copying the gathered weights out of the rank-major all-gather buffer, the wqkv/wo/w13/w2/lm_head GEMMs and the norms read their operand tiles straight from the 8 per-rank chunks, removing the unpack copies entirely.
regions.bitwise_notes: GEMM must accept a chunked operand (8 base pointers / TMA descriptors); results bitwise equal if the GEMM's K-order is unchanged.
regions.dataflow: all_gather output -> (copy) -> weight -> mm. The copy has a single consumer per parameter.
regions.blockers: Needs a GEMM that takes a rank-chunked B operand (grouped/TMA multi-descriptor), and for w13 the Shard(1) chunks interleave within each of the gate/up halves; the backward GEMMs also reuse the unpacked weights, so the copy must either stay or both forward and backward GEMMs read the chunked buffer (which must then stay alive).
regions.notes: Ideal 0: the GEMMs read the weights anyway. Includes the lm_head+norm bucket unpack (1 instance).

regions.title: Attention-backward postprocess fused with RoPE backward and d_qkv concat
regions.description: The attention backward converts its fp32 dq/dk/dv accumulators to bf16 in three postprocess kernels, after which RoPE backward re-casts dq/dk to fp32, rotates, casts back and concatenates into d_qkv; the postprocess can apply the inverse rotation and write d_qkv [8192,8,6,128] directly.
regions.bitwise_notes: Bitwise only if the epilogue reproduces the bf16 rounding of dq/dk before the fp32 rotation.
regions.dataflow: flash_bwd -> postprocess (dq,dk,dv -> bf16) -> _to_copy f32 -> mul(conj freqs) -> _to_copy bf16 -> cat -> wqkv backward GEMMs.
regions.blockers: Attention library internals (flash_attn cute postprocess kernels); needs a custom epilogue hook.
regions.notes: Assumes all three postprocess kernels convert fp32 accumulators (GQA dK/dV accumulate in fp32 in deterministic mode).

regions.title: wqkv GEMM epilogue emitting rotated q/k and contiguous v
regions.description: The wqkv projection [8192,4096]x[4096,6144] can apply RoPE in its epilogue and store q, k, v in the contiguous per-head layouts attention consumes, removing the 10 prologue kernels.
regions.bitwise_notes: Bitwise if the epilogue rounds the accumulator to bf16 before the fp32 rotation, matching the unfused rounding points.
regions.dataflow: mm(wqkv) -> split/clone -> rope -> attention.
regions.blockers: The backward needs the rotated q/k (saved for attention backward) - unchanged; needs a GEMM with a custom epilogue and positional table input.
regions.notes: GEMM measured below the random-data peak, so the gap is GEMM-ideal-relative.

regions.title: RoPE forward: q/k/v contiguous copies + fp32 complex rotation of q and k
regions.description: Each attention splits the wqkv output [8192,6144] bf16 into q/k/v, makes each contiguous, gathers the rotary table for the positions, and rotates q [8192,32,128] and k [8192,8,128] via cast-to-fp32, complex multiply and cast-back (10 kernels); one kernel can read the qkv rows once and write rotated q, k and contiguous v.
regions.bitwise_notes: Casts and complex multiply only; the fused kernel must evaluate the complex product with the same operation order/FMA contraction as aten's complex mul in fp32.
regions.dataflow: mm(wqkv) -> view/split -> clone(q), clone(k), clone(v) -> _to_copy f32 -> view_as_complex -> mul(freqs[index(positions)]) -> view_as_real -> _to_copy bf16 -> _varlen_attn. The three clones and two rotations are siblings over the same qkv rows.
regions.blockers: The rotary table gather is done per layer from the same positions; a fused kernel should take positions + table directly. Attention needs contiguous q/k/v in this layout (varlen packed).
regions.notes: Overlaps the wqkv-epilogue (T3) and the rotary-table CSE regions.

regions.title: RoPE backward: inverse rotation of dq/dk + concat into d_qkv
regions.description: Each attention backward rotates dq [8192,32,128] and dk [8192,8,128] by the conjugate rotary table (cast to fp32, materialize conj, complex multiply, cast back) and concatenates dq/dk/dv into the [8192,8,6,128] wqkv-output gradient (9 kernels); one kernel can read dq/dk/dv once and write d_qkv.
regions.bitwise_notes: Casts + complex multiply with the conjugated table; same rounding points as the aten chain.
regions.dataflow: _varlen_attn_backward -> (dq, dk, dv) -> _to_copy f32 -> mul(conj(freqs) cloned) -> _to_copy bf16 -> cat(dim=heads-group) -> wqkv backward GEMMs.
regions.blockers: None structural.
regions.notes: Overlaps the attention-backward-postprocess (T3) and the rotary-table CSE regions.

regions.title: lm_head weight-gradient fp32 cast fused into the per-chunk wgrad GEMM epilogue
regions.description: For each loss chunk, the lm_head weight gradient [128256,4096] is produced in bf16 by a GEMM and then cast to fp32 for the reduce-scatter by a separate 3.15GB-traffic kernel; the GEMM epilogue can round to bf16 and store fp32 directly.
regions.bitwise_notes: Bitwise if the epilogue rounds the fp32 accumulator to bf16 before widening to fp32.
regions.dataflow: mm(dlogits^T, h) bf16 -> _to_copy f32 -> reduce_scatter -> add_ (accumulate across chunks).
regions.blockers: Needs a GEMM epilogue with custom rounding; the reduce-scatter per chunk (8x the gradient traffic) is itself a structural cost of chunking the loss before reduce-scatter.
regions.notes: Measured GEMM time is below the random-data peak (low-entropy data), so the fused ideal (GEMM at peak) is conservative.

regions.title: RMSNorm backward + residual-gradient accumulation add
regions.description: At every attention_norm and ffn_norm backward ([8192,4096] bf16), the normalized-input gradient is written out and then added to the residual-stream gradient by a separate kernel; one kernel can compute the norm backward and add the incoming residual gradient before writing.
regions.shapes_dtypes: dy, x, residual-grad bf16 [8192,4096]; rstd f32 [8192,1]; weight bf16 [4096] -> dx bf16 [8192,4096], dweight bf16 [4096]
regions.bitwise_notes: Row reductions (dy*w*x dot) and the column reduction for dweight must keep quack's reduction order; the residual add is a bf16 pointwise epilogue on the rounded dx.
regions.dataflow: mm(dgrad of w13 or wqkv) -> _fused_rms_norm_backward -> dx -> add(residual grad, dx) -> next GEMMs. The add's other input is the running residual-stream gradient; dx has no other consumer.
regions.blockers: The add is created by autograd's gradient accumulation (multiple uses of the residual tensor), outside any module; the norm backward is a CuTe DSL kernel (quack) so the add must become its epilogue.
regions.notes: The first instance (layers.31 FFN residual) also absorbs the final norm's backward, whose dx feeds the same add.

regions.title: FSDP all-gather unpack: split_with_sizes_copy + w13 re-layout cat
regions.description: After each block's weight all-gather, the rank-major bf16 buffer [8,27264000] is copied out into six per-parameter tensors, and the w13 weight is then copied a second time from rank-major [16,1792,4096] into [2,14336,4096]; a single copy can write every parameter, including w13, directly in its final layout.
regions.bitwise_notes: Pure data movement; exact element placement (rank-major chunks, Shard(1) for w13) must be reproduced.
regions.dataflow: all_gather_into_tensor_out -> wait -> view [8,-1] -> split_with_sizes_copy(out=6 buffers) -> (w13) split(2) -> cat(dim1) -> reshape [28672,4096] -> mm. Each output is consumed only by its parameter's GEMM/norm.
regions.blockers: Unpack is generated by the bucketing pass and the w13 re-layout by DTensor Shard(1) redistribution; fusing needs the w13 placement known to the unpack.
regions.notes: Weights stay unsharded through backward (memory_policy none), so there is no backward all-gather unpack.

regions.title: Residual add in the wo / w2 GEMM epilogues
regions.description: The attention output projection (wo) and the FFN down projection (w2) each write [8192,4096] bf16 that is immediately added to the residual stream; the GEMM epilogue can add the residual and write h directly.
regions.bitwise_notes: Bitwise if the epilogue rounds the accumulator to bf16 before adding the residual (aten adds two bf16 tensors).
regions.dataflow: mm(wo or w2) -> add(residual, .) -> h -> norm.
regions.blockers: Competes with the add+RMSNorm fusions for the same add; the norm needs the whole row, which a GEMM tile of N=4096 rarely covers.
regions.notes: Ideal per instance is the mean of the two GEMMs' compute ideals; GEMMs measured slightly below that ideal.

regions.title: Token-embedding backward: zero-fill, deterministic scatter-add, fp32 cast and bucket copy
regions.description: The embedding weight gradient [128256,4096] is zero-filled in bf16, scatter-added from the [8192,4096] token gradients via sort/segment kernels, cast to fp32 and then copied again into the reduce-scatter buffer; one pass can write the fp32 bucket directly (zeros for untouched rows, segment sums for touched rows).
regions.bitwise_notes: Deterministic segment sums (sorted by token id) must keep the same per-row accumulation order and the bf16 rounding before widening.
regions.dataflow: embedding_dense_backward (memset 1.05GB, radix sort, compute_grad_weight, sum_and_scatter) -> _to_copy f32 -> _pre_bucket_reduce_scatter (chunk_cat) -> reduce_scatter.
regions.blockers: Deterministic-algorithms mode selects the sort-based embedding backward; the bucket pack is from the bucketing pass.

regions.title: Attention-backward accumulator zero-fill folded into the preprocess kernel
regions.description: Each attention backward launches five memsets (two 51MB fp32 accumulators and three small buffers) before its preprocess kernel (rowsum of dO*O); the preprocess kernel can zero the accumulators in the same pass.
regions.shapes_dtypes: memsets 2x51380224 B + 3x278528 B; preprocess reads O,dO bf16 [8192,32,128], writes f32 [32,8192]
regions.bitwise_notes: Inside the attention library; zero-fill is exact.
regions.dataflow: memset(dq_accum), memset(dk/dv accum), memset(semaphores) ; flash_bwd_preprocess(O, dO) -> flash_bwd.
regions.blockers: Attention library internals (flash_attn cute); requires a library change.
regions.notes: Footprint op is the attention-backward op; only its memset and preprocess kernels are members.

regions.title: lm_head per-chunk reduce-scattered gradient accumulation folded into the reduce-scatter
regions.description: The fp32 lm_head gradient shard [16032,4096] reduce-scattered for each loss chunk is added into a running fp32 accumulator by a separate kernel (7 times); the reduce-scatter's own reduction can take the accumulator as one more operand.
regions.source: torchtitan/experiments/graph_trainer/chunked_loss.py (chunk loop, lm_head grad reduce-scatter per chunk)
regions.bitwise_notes: Changes where the add happens inside the reduction; bitwise only if the accumulator is added after the cross-rank sum, in the same order.
regions.dataflow: reduce_scatter(chunk i) -> wait -> add_(acc, .) -> ... -> final grad.
regions.blockers: Requires a reduce-scatter with an accumulate-into-output epilogue (not available in NCCL); alternatively accumulate the 8 chunk wgrads in fp32 before a single reduce-scatter, which changes summation order (not bitwise) but removes 7 of 8 reduce-scatters.
regions.notes: Ideal assumes the collective reads the accumulator once more (262.7MB); this is a model, not a measurement of a fused kernel.

regions.title: Rotary table gather and conjugate computed once per step instead of per layer
regions.description: Every layer's attention gathers the same [8192,64] complex rotary rows for the same positions in forward, and every layer's backward materializes the same conjugated table twice (for dq and dk); computing the gathered table and its conjugate once per step removes 95 of 96 kernels.
regions.bitwise_notes: Gather and conjugation are exact.
regions.dataflow: index(freqs_cis, positions) per layer (identical inputs) ; _conj -> clone per q/k per layer (identical).
regions.blockers: Each layer's rope module traces its own gather; a graph pass must recognize identical inputs (same placeholder table and positions).
regions.notes: Absorbed automatically if the fused RoPE kernels read positions + table directly.

regions.title: Attention residual add + ffn_norm
regions.description: In each decoder block, h = x + attn_out ([8192,4096] bf16) is written and immediately re-read by ffn_norm; one kernel can add, write h (still needed as residual and for backward), and write the normalized output and rstd.
regions.bitwise_notes: RMSNorm row reduction order must match quack's kernel; the add is bf16 pointwise ahead of it.
regions.dataflow: mm(wo) -> add(x, .) -> h -> _fused_rms_norm(h) -> w13 GEMM; h also feeds the next residual add.
regions.blockers: Norm is a library CuTe DSL kernel; fused add+norm variant needed.
regions.notes: T3 alternative: fold the residual add into the wo GEMM epilogue (see residual-epilogue region).

regions.title: FFN residual add + next layer's attention_norm (final norm after layer 31)
regions.description: The block output out = h + ffn_out ([8192,4096] bf16) is written by one kernel and re-read by the next block's attention_norm (or the final norm); one kernel can do both across the layer boundary.
regions.bitwise_notes: Same as the intra-layer add+norm.
regions.dataflow: mm(w2) -> add(h, .) -> out -> next layer _fused_rms_norm(out) -> wqkv GEMM; out also feeds the next residual add.
regions.blockers: The next layer's FSDP all-gather unpack sits between the two ops in program order (no data dependency).

regions.title: FSDP all-gather input packs (fp32 shard -> bf16 slice) batched into one launch per step
regions.description: Before every block's weight all-gather, its fp32 parameter shards are cast to bf16 into this rank's slice of the gather buffer by one multi-tensor kernel per bucket (34 per step, about 1.3x roofline each); since all shards are available at step start, the 34 casts can run as one multi-tensor launch.
regions.bitwise_notes: fp32 -> bf16 casts only (round-to-nearest-even, identical in any kernel).
regions.dataflow: param shard (placeholder) -> _pre_bucket_all_gather (cast + copy into slice) -> all_gather_into_tensor_out (in place). The 34 packs have no data dependencies on each other or on the forward.
regions.blockers: All 34 gather output buffers (436MB each per layer) would be allocated at step start instead of just before each layer's all-gather; with memory_policy 'none' they all stay alive until backward anyway, so peak memory changes little, but the bucketing pass emits one pack per bucket by construction.
regions.notes: Small: the gap is launch and tail overhead of 34 separate multi-tensor launches. A further step would write the bf16 copy in the previous step's optimizer update (out of scope).

regions.title: lm_head input-gradient written in place into the hidden-state gradient buffer
regions.description: Each chunk's lm_head input gradient [1024,4096] bf16 is produced by a GEMM and then copied into a zero-initialized [8192,4096] buffer; the GEMM can write its rows of the buffer directly and the zero-fill is unnecessary because the 8 chunks cover all rows.
regions.bitwise_notes: Writing the GEMM result to a row slice is bitwise identical.
regions.dataflow: zeros_like(h) ; mm(dlogits, W) -> copy_ into slice [i*1024:(i+1)*1024] -> final norm backward.
regions.blockers: The copy is generated by the chunked loss's manual gradient assembly; the zero-fill is only removable if every row is provably written.
regions.notes: These ops are tagged as forward in the graph (they run in the loss module's forward, outside autograd's backward).

regions.title: Token-embedding gather + layer-0 attention_norm
regions.description: The embedding gather writes the [8192,4096] bf16 hidden state and layer 0's attention_norm re-reads it; one kernel can gather rows, write the residual and the normalized output.
regions.bitwise_notes: Norm reduction order as quack; the gather is exact.
regions.dataflow: embedding(table, ids) -> h0 -> _fused_rms_norm -> wqkv GEMM; h0 also the residual.
regions.blockers: None structural; tiny.
regions.notes: The embedding gather itself measured below its byte roofline (repeated token rows hit in L2).

regions.title: Final norm weight-gradient fp32 cast + reduce-scatter bucket copy
regions.description: The final norm's 4096-element bf16 weight gradient is cast to fp32 and then copied into its own reduce-scatter bucket by a second kernel (plus a host-to-device metadata copy); one kernel can write the fp32 bucket directly.
regions.bitwise_notes: Exact cast + copy.
regions.dataflow: _fused_rms_norm_backward (dweight) -> _to_copy f32 -> _pre_bucket_reduce_scatter -> reduce_scatter.
regions.blockers: Launch-bound; a better fix is putting this 4096-element parameter in the same bucket as lm_head (both are packed separately today).
regions.notes: Pure launch overhead.

no_opportunity.what: Attention forward internal memsets (3 tiny zero-fills per layer inside the attention op)
no_opportunity.reason: Inside the attention library; ~2.4us per layer of launch-bound memsets. Same fix as the backward memset region (fold into the main kernel), negligible size; listed for completeness.

no_opportunity.what: Post-backward gradient accumulation clone into .grad (outside the graph, after backward)
no_opportunity.reason: Out of scope (after backward). Would be removable by letting the reduce-scatter write directly into .grad.
